reconcile.connective: Defenders read the singular "but my servant Caleb" not as exclusive but as a partial naming, with Joshua excepted too and named in the very same chapter and the later musters.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells, compiler of the Skeptic's Annotated Bible, presses the wording at face value: Numbers 14:24 swears that of the doomed generation only Caleb will see the land, yet the surrounding passages list Caleb and Joshua as the two survivors.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.work: Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "Who survived to see the promised land during the Exodus?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/caleb.html)

excerpts.excerpt_text: Joshua was also excepted, but he is not named because he was no longer in the ranks of the people, being a constant attendant on Moses.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly states that Joshua was 'also excepted' and gives the contextual reason the oath at 14:24 names only Caleb — the core harmonization of singular-Caleb vs Caleb-and-Joshua.

excerpts.excerpt_text: just as Joshua also is not mentioned in this place, as he is at Num 14:30 and Num 14:38, but Caleb only … This first revelation of God to Moses is restricted to the main fact …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Names both later verses (14:30, 14:38) where Joshua appears and supplies the harmonizing principle — the first oath is 'restricted to the main fact,' so the omission of Joshua at 14:24 is not exclusion.

excerpts.excerpt_text: Here Joshua is set first, as Caleb is in Num 14:30; which shows that they were equal in dignity …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Reads the later passages as confirming Joshua and Caleb stood on equal footing as the two survivors, so the singular naming at 14:24 cannot mean Caleb alone survived.

pd_work.resource: Jamieson, Fausset & Brown, Commentary Critical and Explanatory on the Whole Bible (1871), on Numbers 14:24
pd_work.author: Jamieson, Fausset & Brown
pd_work.note: Treats this exact passage, stating Joshua was 'also excepted' though not named at 14:24, which harmonizes the singular oath with the later passages naming both survivors.

link.title: GotQuestions: Who was Caleb in the Bible?
link.note: Live apologetic treatment; presents Caleb and Joshua as the only two of their generation to survive and enter Canaan, citing Numbers 14:11-24 and the 'different spirit' that singles Caleb out.
